prime.problem: A freshly initialised net can start out confidently wrong, and a loss curve that still goes down hides it: you spend the first stretch of training just undoing the bad init, and you never notice.
prime.fits: First card of the BatchNorm lecture. It reuses the z2h-4 MLP and its cross-entropy loss, and turns that loss into a diagnostic you can read before training starts.
prime.goal: Say what loss any V-class model should print at step 0, read a much higher number as a mis-scaled output layer, and check it on your own MLP.

attend: Why does a model that knows nothing have a loss of exactly ln 27, and not 0 or infinity?
In the 4-class toy, what makes [0, 0, 5, 0] cost more than [0, 0, 0, 0], when neither logit vector knows the answer?
Which two parameters of the starter MLP set the scale of its logits, and why does std-1 randn make that scale about 13?
Why can a step-0 loss near 3.30 still hide a badly initialised hidden layer?

must: Loss = −ln p(correct), averaged → a model with no information spreads p evenly → p = 1/V for every example → the step-0 target is ln V (ln 27 = 3.2958 here)

Large logits → softmax puts almost all probability on one class → without knowledge that class is usually wrong → p(correct) tiny → the loss grows with the logit scale (≈10 at ×10, ≈103 at ×100 in the toy) and has no ceiling
W2, b2 drawn with std 1 and 200 hidden units near ±1 → logit std ≈ √(200·0.846 + 1) ≈ 13 → confident random bets → step-0 loss 27.8817 instead of 3.2958 → early training is wasted shrinking logits
Step-0 loss ≫ ln V → the output layer is over-scaled → fix the init before training (next card); step-0 loss ≈ ln V → the output layer is fine, but the hidden layer still needs its own check
elevated: The know-nothing baseline ignores class frequencies → a model that only learned character frequencies would score 2.8226 on this data → so a step 0 slightly above 3.2958 is healthy, and getting there is already easy progress for training
reference: the seed 2147483647 and the randn draw order that reproduce 27.8817

compress.prompt: From memory, explain in 3–5 sentences what loss an untrained 27-class model should show, why the starter MLP shows 27.88 instead, and what that tells you to do. Or draw the chain from W2's scale to the step-0 loss.
checklist: knowing nothing means p = 1/27 for every character, so the loss is ln 27 = 3.2958
the loss punishes confidence on the wrong class; big logits make softmax confident
std-1 W2/b2 over 200 hidden units give logits of std about 13, so the net bets hard and mostly wrong
the gap (27.88 vs 3.30) is visible at step 0, before any training
fix: scale the output layer down so logits start near 0 (the next card)

retrieve.q: Explain why ln V is the loss of a model that knows nothing, using the definition of the loss rather than the number.
answer: the loss is the average of −ln p(correct)
knowing nothing, the fairest prediction is equal probability 1/V per class
every term is then −ln(1/V) = ln V, so the average is ln V

retrieve.q: Walk through what happens in softmax and the loss when the logits for 4 classes are [0, 0, 5, 0] and the right class is 0.
Why not simply set W2 and b2 to exactly zero, which gives a perfect 3.2958 at step 0? What do you gain, and what do you risk?
answer: gain: logits are exactly 0, so the loss is exactly ln 27
risk: identical parameters get identical gradients, so symmetry is never broken
Karpathy keeps small nonzero values (×0.01 gives 3.3221), which costs almost nothing in loss

retrieve.q: Your step-0 loss is 3.31 on a 27-class problem. What can you conclude, and what can't you?
answer: can: the output logits are near zero, so the output layer isn't confidently wrong
can't: the hidden layer may still be saturated (tanh near ±1), which this check doesn't see

compare.q: This card detects the bad init and that card fixes it. What single quantity links the two, and why does shrinking W2 move the step-0 loss from 27.88 towards 3.30 without teaching the net anything?
answer: the link is the logit scale
shrinking W2 and zeroing b2 pulls the logits towards 0, so softmax moves towards uniform
uniform is the ln 27 baseline, so the loss drops to it with no new knowledge

compare.q: Both are cheap sanity checks run before a full training run. What does each one prove, and which bug would each one miss?
answer: step-0 loss checks the starting point: is the output scale sane?
overfitting one batch checks capacity and plumbing: can the loss reach near 0 at all?
the step-0 check misses a broken backward pass; overfit-one-batch can still pass with a confidently wrong init (it just takes longer)

predict.q: GPT-2 predicts one of 50,257 tokens. If you build it correctly, what loss should its first training step print, and would a first loss of 11.0 worry you?
predict.answer: ln 50257 = 10.8249 (computed). An 11.0 is slightly above the blind-guess cost, the same healthy "a bit above ln V" you see here with 3.32 vs 3.2958, so it's fine. A first loss of 30 or more would mean the same confidently-wrong output layer as this card. (The z2h-10 first-loss card checks exactly this.)

apply.task: In the Build-it snippet, scale the output layer right after drawing it: W2 = torch.randn(...) * s and b2 = torch.randn(...) * 0. Before running, predict the step-0 loss for s = 0.1, 0.01 and 0, then run all three and compare with ln 27.
apply.done: You get 4.2326, 3.3221 and 3.2958, and can explain why s = 0 hits ln 27 exactly while s = 0.01 lands just above it.
apply.hint: With s = 0 every logit is 0, so softmax is exactly uniform. With s = 0.01 the logits are small but not zero, so they still make small (random) bets.

reflect: Which prediction did you get wrong: the 27.88, or how fast the toy loss grows with the logit scale?
What couldn't you explain cleanly: why confidence is punished, or why std-1 weights give logits of std about 13?
Which relationship is still fuzzy: weight scale → logit scale, or logit scale → loss?
Would you now compute ln V before training any new classifier? What would you do if it didn't match?
What will you look at in the hidden layer before the saturated-tanh card?
